name: Elam
summary: An ancient civilisation of south-western Iran, centred on Susa. Its kingdoms were long rivals of Sumer, Babylon and Assyria, and its administration later shaped Persian government.

location.value: Far west and south-west Iran (Ilam and Khuzestan) and a small part of southern Iraq.

terrain.value: The Khuzestan lowlands and the Zagros mountains.

climate.value: Hot lowlands in Khuzestan and cooler highlands in the Zagros Mountains.

resources.value: Farmland, timber, stone and metals from the highlands.

urbanisation.value: Susa in the lowlands and Anshan in the highlands were the main cities.

migration.value: Iranian-speaking peoples migrated into the region in the 1st millennium BCE, pushing Elam back towards the Susa plain.
migration.source: Potts, The Archaeology of Elam (2016); Encyclopaedia Iranica: Elam i. The history of Elam (checked 14 Nov 2026)

economicBase.value: Farming and trade between Mesopotamia and the Iranian plateau.

tradeRoutes.value: Routes to Mesopotamia and across the Iranian plateau to Central Asia.

moneyAndTax.value: No coinage; silver was used by weight.

inequality.value: Kings, nobles and temple elites above farmers.

governmentType.value: Monarchy with an unusual system of shared rule among royal relatives.

keyRulers.value: Untash-Napirisha (built Chogha Zanbil), Shutruk-Nakhunte (took the Code of Hammurabi stele to Susa).
keyRulers.source: Potts, The Archaeology of Elam (2016); Encyclopaedia Iranica: Elam i. The history of Elam (checked 14 Nov 2026)

succession.value: Usually the eldest son took the throne, but the mother mattered: sons of a royal sister or daughter ranked above sons of foreign princesses, and a side branch could take over if there was no suitable heir.
succession.source: Potts, The Archaeology of Elam (2016); Encyclopaedia Iranica: Elam i. The history of Elam (checked 14 Nov 2026)

institutions.value: Administrative traditions that became a foundation of the Iranian system.

stability.value: Conquered and revived several times over more than 2,000 years.

majorWars.value: Wars with Sumer, Akkad, Babylon; Assyria sacked Susa (about 647–646 BCE).
majorWars.source: Potts, The Archaeology of Elam (2016); Encyclopaedia Iranica: Elam i. The history of Elam (checked 14 Nov 2026)

territoryChange.value: Expanded and shrank many times; in the 12th century BCE Elamite kings raided Babylonia and in 1158 BCE placed a king’s son on the Babylonian throne.
territoryChange.source: Potts, The Archaeology of Elam (2016); Encyclopaedia Iranica: Elam i. The history of Elam (checked 14 Nov 2026)

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals of the Mesopotamian states (Sumer, Akkad, Babylon, Assyria).

inventions.value: Proto-Elamite writing (about 3100 BCE), one of the oldest scripts, still undeciphered.

scienceEducation.value: Scribes wrote in Elamite and Akkadian.

openness.value: Used Mesopotamian cuneiform and traded widely.

communicationTransport.value: Roads linking Susa with the Iranian highlands; donkeys and pack animals; river transport in the lowlands.

religion.value: Elamite gods such as Inshushinak, protector of Susa.
religion.source: Potts, The Archaeology of Elam (2016); Encyclopaedia Iranica: Elam i. The history of Elam (checked 14 Nov 2026)

languageWriting.value: Written records from around 3000 BCE; Elamite language (an isolate).

artsArchitecture.value: The ziggurat of Chogha Zanbil (about 1250 BCE), a World Heritage Site.
artsArchitecture.source: Potts, The Archaeology of Elam (2016); Encyclopaedia Iranica: Elam i. The history of Elam, date of Chogha Zanbil only (checked 14 Nov 2026)

socialStructure.value: Kings, priests, scribes, craftspeople and farmers.

sharedIdentity.value: The Elamite language and gods such as Inshushinak.

dailyLife.value: Mud-brick houses in towns; farming of barley and wheat in the lowlands, herding in the highlands.

neighbours.value: Sumer, Akkad, Babylon, Assyria and Persia.

ideasReligions.value: Elamite administration shaped early Iranian government.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Elam (checked 6 Nov 2026); Potts, The Archaeology of Elam (2016)

riseSignals.value: Early towns appeared in Khuzestan in the 4th millennium BCE.

declineSignals.value: The Assyrian king Ashurbanipal sacked Susa (about 647–646 BCE), though Elam recovered afterwards and the damage was less than his own records claim.
declineSignals.source: Potts, The Archaeology of Elam (2016); Encyclopaedia Iranica: Elam i. The history of Elam (checked 14 Nov 2026)

outcome.value: Absorbed into the Achaemenid Persian Empire.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Elam (checked 6 Nov 2026); Encyclopaedia Iranica: Elam i. The history of Elam (checked 14 Nov 2026)

overallCertainty.value: Medium; the writing is only partly understood. Second source: Wikidata starts c. 2700 BCE; Wikipedia gives 3200 BCE.
